title: Marketplace Partner API Reference
snippet:
When a user interacts with your integration, Vercel calls your Partner API endpoints on your integration server. You implement these endpoints to handle:
- **Installation lifecycle** — Create, update, and delete installations when users add or remove your integration
- **Resource management** — Provision and configure resources when users connect projects or add configuration
- **Billing operations** — Handle invoice creation, usage reporting, and payment processing
- **User authentication** — Validate and process user-initiated actions

Of the 18 endpoints in the Partner API spec, 6 are required for every integration. The remaining 12 are optional and unlocked by specific features your integration supports. When getting started, implement the 6 required endpoints first, then add optional ones as your feature set grows.

| [Upsert Installation](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api/reference/partner/upsert-installation) | Required | Vercel calls this endpoint when a customer [installs your integration](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-flows), sending credentials (access token), scopes, and account info. Store the installation ID, configure the account on your side, and save the access token for calling Vercel APIs. |

title: Requirements for listing an Integration
snippet:
The Redirect URL is an HTTP endpoint that handles the installation process by exchanging a code for an API token, serving a user interface, and managing project connections:
- Token Exchange: Exchanges a provided code for a [Vercel REST API access token](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/vercel-api-integrations#exchange-code-for-access-token)
- User Interface: Displays a responsive UI in a popup window during the installation
- Project Provisioning: Allows users to create new projects or connect existing ones in your system to their Vercel Projects
- Completion: Redirects the user back to Vercel upon successful installation

API Scopes define the level of access your integration will have to the Vercel REST API. When setting up a new integration, you need to:
- Select only the API Scopes that are essential for your integration to function
- Choose the appropriate permission level for each scope: `None`, `Read`, or `Read/Write`

Before you can publish, you must accept the partner terms that match how customers use your integration:
| Integration type | How customers use your integration | Applicable partner terms |
|---|---|---|
| [Native integration](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations#native-integrations) | Customers pick plans for your products in the Vercel dashboard, and Vercel bills them through their Vercel account. | The Integrations Agreement covers the marketplace partner program for native billing, including charges, payouts, and how you list products. That program builds on the [Vercel Integrations Marketplace Agreement](https://vercel.com/legal/integrations-marketplace-agreement). |
| [Connectable account integration](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations#connectable-accounts) | Customers link an existing account with your service. Vercel does not sell or renew your product subscription as part of the native installation flow. | The [Vercel Integrations Marketplace Agreement](https://vercel.com/legal/integrations-marketplace-agreement), which governs listing and distributing your integration on the Integrations Marketplace. |

title: Vercel Connect
snippet:
Give your agents and services short-lived access to Slack, GitHub, Microsoft, Snowflake, and other OAuth or API-key services, without storing provider secrets in your environment variables.

With [Vercel Connect](https://vercel.com/connect), your deployed apps can talk to other services. First, you set up a connection once to Slack, GitHub, Microsoft, Snowflake, Salesforce, or any OAuth or API-key service at the team level. Then, any project you allow can use this connection. Your code asks Connect for access at the moment it needs it, so no provider API key ever lives in your environment variables.

- Vercel OIDC token (recommended): On Vercel, the SDK uses the [OIDC token](https://vercel.com/docs/oidc) that Vercel injects into your deployment automatically. Connect verifies the token and checks it against the connector's project links to confirm your project and environment are allowed to request tokens.
- Access token: For external CI/CD or non-Vercel environments where `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` isn't available, pass a [Vercel access token](https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api#creating-an-access-token) to the SDK through the `vercelToken` option on `getToken`. Dashboard and CLI calls authenticate the same way, using your active Vercel session.

Vercel Connect is billed per token request. Hobby includes 500 token requests per month at no extra charge. Pro is billed at $3.00 per 1,000 token requests. Enterprise is billed at your negotiated Enterprise rate. Contact your account team for details. See [Pricing](https://vercel.com/docs/connect/pricing) for the full table and how to stop being billed.

title: Vercel for Startups
snippet:
Applications are evaluated using the following criteria:
- Startup must be affiliated with an approved Startups Partner (see full dropdown list above). This typically includes companies in accelerators, those backed by Venture Capital firms, or startups that meet certain criteria set by Vercel.
- Startup must not have previously received Vercel for Startups credits.
- Startup must have raised a Series A or less, and must apply within 12 months from their most recent funding round.
- Startup must have a company website, and an email address that matches the company website.
- Startup must have proof (screenshot of partner dashboard, hub, wiki, or console) demonstrating affiliation with an approved Vercel for Startups partner.

To apply for Vercel for Startups, visit [vercel.com/startups/credits](https://vercel.com/startups/credits) and fill out the application form. You'll need to provide your email, select or create a Vercel team, choose your startup partner, and upload proof of partnership. Our team will review your application and get back to you within 5-7 days. If approved, you'll be prompted to review and accept the Flexible Commitment for Startups Terms, at which point your credits and Enterprise access go live within 5-7 business days.

The Vercel for Startups program is an exclusive offer to companies backed by our Startup Partners. If you don’t see your partner listed here, please reach out to your VC to submit a partner request form on [vercel.com/startups/partners](https://vercel.com/startups/partners/#partner-form).

title: Using the Integrations REST API
snippet:
- Vercel calls the provider API: You implement the [Vercel Marketplace Partner API](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api/reference/partner) endpoints on your integration server. Vercel calls them to manage resources, handle installations, and process billing.
- The provider calls the Vercel API: Vercel provides [these endpoints](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api/reference/vercel). You call them from your integration server to interact with Vercel's platform.

Authenticate your integration's calls to the Vercel API with short-lived access tokens, which expire after one hour.

This guidance applies to:
- User authentication JWT tokens received when [Vercel calls your API](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api/reference/partner#user-authentication)
- Tokens received through the [SSO Token Exchange](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api/reference/vercel/exchange-sso-token) endpoint
- Member information returned from the [Get Member](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api/reference/vercel/get-member) endpoint

When Supports Installation Billing Plans is enabled in the Integration Console, Vercel calls the [Get Installation](https://vercel.com/docs/integrations/create-integration/marketplace-api/reference/partner/get-installation) endpoint (`GET /v1/installations/{installationId}`) on your integration server to fetch the installation state.
